SHMI and SHMI+

Source: vignettes/articles/SHMI.Rmd
SHMI.Rmd

A Weighted Sum of Three Management Sub-indices, plus an Organic Amendment Bonus

Overview

The Soil Health Management Index reports two 0–100 scores. SHMI combines Cover, Diversity and Inverse Disturbance, with weights calibrated against measured soil health. SHMI+ adds a bonus for organic amendments.

1. The formulas

For management unit ii:

SHMIi=0.687Coveri+0.150Diversityi+0.163InvDisti \text{SHMI}_i = 0.687\,\text{Cover}_i + 0.150\,\text{Diversity}_i + 0.163\,\text{InvDist}_i

SHMI+i=SHMIi+0.60pamend,i(100−SHMIi) \text{SHMI+}_i = \text{SHMI}_i + 0.60\,p_{amend,i}\,(100 - \text{SHMI}_i)

where pamend,ip_{amend,i} is the share of years with an organic amendment.

Constant Value 95% range across 1,000 calibration fits
Cover weight 0.687 0.65 – 0.73
Diversity weight 0.150 fixed
Inverse Disturbance weight 0.163 0.12 – 0.20
Growing-season share in Cover 0.760 0.70 – 0.83
Grazing share (Diversity) 0.25 chosen; fit flat 0.25 – 0.5
Amendment share (SHMI+) 0.60 chosen; fit flat 0.5 – 0.8

The weights sum to 1 and both gap terms close part of the distance to 100, so 0≤SHMIi≤SHMI+i≤1000 \le \text{SHMI}_i \le \text{SHMI+}_i \le 100. shmi_weights() returns the weights and shmi_parameters() every constant.

2. How build_shmi() computes them

  1. Validation. The inputs from prepare_shmi_inputs() are checked: required tables and columns, valid dates, unique MGT_combo, and tillage values that suit the tillage scale.
  2. Tillage. Computed as in USDA’s T-DISC tool, from implement mixing efficiencies and depths (from the pass, a user table, or T-DISC); STIR records with dist_meth = "STIR".
  3. Sub-indices. shmi_components() computes the sub-indices over each unit’s evaluation window, using the monthly climate for Cover, and the shares of years with amendments and with animals; grazing raises Diversity. Missing records mean the practice did not happen.
  4. Combination. SHMI is the weighted sum; SHMI+ adds the amendment bonus.

3. Official and custom scores

Scores are official when the official weights and constants are used, with either tillage scale. Custom weights (rescaled to sum to 1), growing_share, graze_gap or amend_gap (for research or scenario analysis) flag the result official = FALSE.

4. Output

build_shmi() returns a list. Its indicator_df has one row per management unit:

Column Range Meaning
SHMI 0–100 weighted sum of the three sub-indices
SHMI_plus 0–100 SHMI plus the amendment bonus
Amend_bonus 0–60 SHMI_plus − SHMI
Cover, Diversity, InvDist 0–100 the sub-indices (Diversity with the grazing credit)
Cover_growing, Cover_nongrowing 0–100 the two parts of Cover
Diversity_plants 0–100 Diversity before the grazing credit
Richness species average species per 4-year span
p_amend, p_animal 0–1 shares of years with an organic amendment and with animals
TI_tillage, tillage_designation T-DISC tillage intensity and NT / RT / CT

plus the unit’s study, farm, field and treatment. The list also records weights, parameters, dist_meth, official, shmi_version and timestamp.

Interpretation

  • Higher scores mean management more supportive of soil health: more of the year under living cover, more plant species and grazing, less tillage and, for SHMI+, more frequent organic amendments.
  • Two scores. SHMI describes the field’s own management; SHMI+ adds carbon brought in from outside. They are equal for a unit without amendments.
  • Precision. For US sites not used in calibration, SHMI+ explained about a quarter of the differences in measured soil health (R² = 0.26) and ranked practices in the right order at 82% of sites (SHMI: 0.23 and 76%); a single prediction is typically within about 13 soil-health points. Both are most informative for comparing practices at the same site.
  • Scope. Calibrated on US systems; recalibrate before use in other regions.
